Based on the retrieved standards documentation, the company's projected increase in hazardous waste generation from approximately 600 kg/month to 1,400 kg/month on a sustained basis creates a significant compliance obligation related to its RCRA generator status. This change in operational conditions triggers a re-evaluation of legal requirements under **ISO 14001:2015 clause 6.1.3** and **ISO 45001:2018 clause 6.1.3**.

### **Primary Compliance Obligation Affected:**

**1. RCRA Hazardous Waste Generator Category Upgrade**
*   **Requirement:** The company's status will change from a Small Quantity Generator (SQG) to a Large Quantity Generator (LQG). This upgrade imposes additional duties including: weekly inspections of accumulation areas, personnel training, a contingency plan with a quick-reference guide, a 90-day accumulation limit (instead of 180 days for SQGs), biennial reporting, and no volume cap on waste accumulation. The generator category is set by monthly generation [Doc 1 — clause 6.1.3].
*   **Source:** 40 CFR Part 262, as administered by the Georgia Environmental Protection Division (EPD) under its authorized RCRA program [Doc 1 — clause 6.1.3].
*   **Applicability:** This applies directly because the company's waste volumes are changing with increased production, and a sustained generation of 1,400 kg/month meets the LQG threshold (≥1,000 kg/mo) [Doc 1 — clause 6.1.3].
*   **ISO Mapping:** **ISO 14001:2015 clause 6.1.3** (determination of legal requirements) and **clause 8.1** (operational control). Also maps to **ISO 45001:2018 clause 6.1.3** [Doc 1 — clause 6.1.3].
*   **Evaluation & Timing (per ISO 14001/45001 clause 9.1.2):**
    *   **How:** Compliance should be evaluated by reviewing monthly hazardous waste generation records against the RCRA category thresholds (100 kg/mo and 1,000 kg/mo). An audit must verify that all new LQG requirements (e.g., weekly inspection logs, training records, contingency plan updates, biennial report submission) are implemented.
    *   **When:** Evaluation must occur **immediately** upon the projection of the increased throughput and **before** the start of the next quarter when the 1,400 kg/month generation is expected to begin. The generator category must be re-evaluated each month based on actual generation, and a formal compliance evaluation of the LQG program should be conducted at least annually.

### **Related Compliance Obligations to Re-evaluate:**

The change in operational scale and generator status may also necessitate a review of other obligations in the register:

**2. Hazard Communication (HazCom) Program**
*   **Requirement:** Maintain a written program, chemical inventory, accessible Safety Data Sheets (SDSs), proper container labeling, and employee training [Doc 3 — clause 7.4].
*   **Source:** OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200 [Doc 3 — clause 7.4].
*   **Applicability:** The increased throughput will involve the use of new or greater quantities of hazardous chemicals (solvents, coatings) [Doc 3 — clause 7.4].
*   **ISO Mapping:** **ISO 45001:2018 clause 7.4** (communication) and clauses 7.2/7.3 (competence, awareness) [Doc 3 — clause 7.4].
*   **Evaluation & Timing:** Review and update the chemical inventory and SDS collection. Ensure training is provided to employees before the new production levels begin, as new hazards may be introduced. Evaluate annually or whenever changes occur.

**3. EPCRA Tier II Inventory Reporting**
*   **Requirement:** Submit an annual Tier II inventory report (by March 1) to state/local authorities and the fire department for hazardous chemicals stored at or above 10,000 lbs at any time, or for Extremely Hazardous Substances (EHS) at their Threshold Planning Quantities (TPQ) [Doc 5 — clause 7.4].
*   **Source:** EPCRA §§311/312, 40 CFR Parts 355/370 [Doc 5 — clause 7.4].
*   **Applicability:** Increased production will likely increase on-site inventories of solvents, coatings, and related chemicals (e.g., toluene, acetone). The company must check if these increases cross the 10,000 lb threshold for any chemical or the TPQ for any EHS [Doc 5 — clause 7.4].
*   **ISO Mapping:** **ISO 14001:2015 clause 7.4.3** (external communication) and **ISO 45001:2018 clause 8.2** (emergency preparedness) [Doc 5 — clause 7.4].
*   **Evaluation & Timing:** Re-evaluate chemical inventories **immediately** and upon receiving any new material. Formal evaluation occurs at year-end for the annual March 1 report, but ongoing monitoring is required as inventory levels change.

**4. Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) Form R Reporting**
*   **Requirement:** Facilities in covered NAICS sectors with 10+ employees must report annually (by July 1) if they manufacture, process, or otherwise use listed TRI chemicals above threshold amounts (e.g., 25,000 lb manufactured/processed, 10,000 lb otherwise used) [Doc 6 — clause 9.1.1].
*   **Source:** EPCRA §313, 40 CFR Part 372 [Doc 6 — clause 9.1.1].
*   **Applicability:** Tripling coating throughput may increase the annual "otherwise use" of listed solvents (e.g., toluene, methyl ethyl ketone) or metals in surface treatments past reporting thresholds [Doc 6 — clause 9.1.1].
*   **ISO Mapping:** **ISO 14001:2015 clause 9.1.1** (monitoring, measurement, analysis) [Doc 6 — clause 9.1.1].
*   **Evaluation & Timing:** Track the annual throughput of TRI-listed chemicals. A formal evaluation must be performed at the end of the calendar year to determine if thresholds were exceeded, triggering a July 1 report.

**Summary:** The core new obligation is the **RCRA LQG status upgrade** [Doc 1 — clause 6.1.3]. This change should prompt a review of the compliance register, particularly for obligations tied to chemical usage and inventory (**HazCom** [Doc 3 — clause 7.4], **Tier II** [Doc 5 — clause 7.4], **TRI** [Doc 6 — clause 9.1.1]), as increased production likely affects these areas. Compliance must be evaluated **before** the new production begins and monitored continuously thereafter.
